methods.name: analysis_create
methods.summary: Create and start an analysis by module name and analysis name.

params.name: module
params.description: JASP module name, e.g. 'jaspTTests'.

params.name: analysis
params.description: Analysis name within the module, e.g. 'TTestIndependent'.

result.name: analysis_create_result
result.description: Metadata about the created analysis, including its default options.

status.description: Always 'success' when the analysis was created.

analysisId.description: Unique integer identifier for the new analysis.

options.description: The current default analysis options. This is the same schema used by analysis_run and get_analyses_state.

optionMeta.description: Metadata describing each option: its kind (checkbox/combo/variables/number/string), valid choices for combos, allowed column types for variable lists, whether a variable list accepts single or multiple variables, and a shape example showing valid input.

methods.name: analysis_run
methods.summary: Set options and run an analysis, blocking up to timeoutMs for the R engine to finish. Combines setOptions + results in one call. Use analysis_results to poll if the timeout fires.

params.name: analysisId
params.description: The integer identifier of the analysis to modify.

params.name: options
params.description: An object of option name/value pairs to set on the analysis.

params.name: wait
params.description: If true, blocks the call until the analysis finishes or timeoutMs elapses. If false, returns immediately with status 'running' and no results.

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Maximum milliseconds to wait when wait=true.

params.name: optionMetaDelta
params.description: If true (default), the response carries an optionMetaDelta field containing only the parts of optionMeta that changed since the last analysis_run (or since analysis_create if this is the first run). When nothing has changed optionMetaDelta is omitted entirely. This dramatically reduces response size on repeated calls. Set to false to receive the full optionMeta field instead.

result.name: analysis_run_result
result.description: The results of the analysis after setting options. IMPORTANT: Only call analysis_results to poll if status is 'running' (timeout). If status is 'success' or 'error' the analysis is already done — do NOT re-poll with analysis_results.

status.description: 'success' (finished with results), 'running' (timeout — still computing), or 'error' (options validation failed).

options.description: The current analysis options (present on success and running).

optionMeta.description: Full metadata describing each option (present on success and running when optionMetaDelta is false or omitted).

optionMetaDelta.description: Delta of optionMeta: only the branches that changed since the last analysis_run (or since analysis_create for the first call). Missing keys in the client cache are left unchanged; keys with a value of null signal deletion. Merge this recursively into your cached optionMeta. Omitted entirely when nothing has changed. Only present when optionMetaDelta=true. Note: analysis_create always returns the full optionMeta to seed the cache.

results.description: The full results JSON. Only populated when the analysis reaches a terminal state (complete, validationError, or fatalError). Empty object otherwise.

jaspResultsRds.description: Absolute path to results in RDS format, only usable from R. Only available when JSON results are present too.

methods.name: get_analyses_state
methods.summary: Retrieve current state for one or more analyses: options and optionally results. Use this to observe the current workspace state before mutating it, or whenever you need a complete snapshot of specific analyses.

params.name: analysisIds
params.description: Array of analysis IDs to query.

params.name: include_options
params.description: If true (default), include the current bound options and optionMeta for each analysis.

params.name: options_meta_diff
params.description: If true (default), return only the changed keys in optionMeta (a diff against the last baseline). On the first call for an analysis the full meta is returned and the baseline is seeded. If false, the full optionMeta is always returned.

params.name: include_results
params.description: If true, include the full results JSON for each finished analysis. Defaults to false because results can be large.

params.name: include_descriptions
params.description: If true, include human-readable description text in optionMeta. Defaults to false to save tokens.

result.name: get_analyses_state_result
result.description: Current state for the requested analyses.

analyses.description: One entry per requested analysis ID, in request order.

status.description: Analysis lifecycle: empty, running, complete, validationError, fatalError, aborted, etc.

options.description: Current bound options. Present when include_options is true.

optionMeta.description: Full option metadata. Present when include_options is true and options_meta_diff is false.

optionMetaDelta.description: Changed keys only (null signals a deletion). Present when include_options is true and options_meta_diff is true. Omitted entirely when nothing changed.

results.description: Full results JSON. Present when include_results is true and the analysis is finished; null otherwise.

missing.description: Requested IDs that no longer exist.

methods.name: analysis_results
methods.summary: Poll for results of an analysis, blocking up to timeoutMs. ONLY call this after analysis_run returned status 'running' (timeout). Do NOT call if analysis_run already returned 'success' or 'error' — the results are already final.

params.name: analysisId
params.description: The integer identifier of the analysis to query.

params.name: wait
params.description: If true, blocks the call until the analysis finishes or timeoutMs elapses. If false, returns immediately with status 'running' and no results.

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Maximum milliseconds to wait when wait=true.

result.name: analysis_results_result
result.description: The current results of the analysis.

results.description: The full results JSON of the analysis. Returns an empty object when the analysis has not yet finished (i.e., status is still computing/aborting/etc.). Only populated once the analysis reaches a terminal state: complete, validationError, or fatalError.

jaspResultsRds.description: Absolute path to results in RDS format, only usable from R. Only available when JSON results are present too.

methods.name: analysis_context
methods.summary: Retrieve context for an analysis: help text and metadata. Intended for AI clients that need to understand what an analysis does and what options are available.

params.name: module
params.description: JASP module name, e.g. 'jaspTTests'.

params.name: analysis
params.description: Analysis name within the module, e.g. 'TTestIndependentSamples'.

result.name: analysis_context_result
result.description: The analysis help text in Markdown format, if available.

help.description: The analysis help text in Markdown format, or empty string if no help file exists for this analysis.

methods.name: modules_list
methods.summary: List all loaded modules and their available analyses.

title.description: Human-readable analysis title, e.g. 'Independent Samples T-Test'.

methods.name: analyses_list
methods.summary: List all analyses currently in the workspace.

activeAnalysisId.description: The ID of the currently selected analysis, or -1 if none is selected.

analyses.description: All analyses currently in the workspace.

methods.name: data_load
methods.summary: Load a data file into the workspace. Blocks up to timeoutMs when wait=true.

params.name: path
params.description: Absolute path to the data file (CSV, SPSS, JASP, Excel, etc.).

params.name: wait
params.description: If true, blocks until the load finishes or timeoutMs elapses. If false, returns immediately with a jobId for polling.

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Maximum milliseconds to wait when wait=true.

params.name: delimiter
params.description: CSV delimiter character. Defaults to comma. Skips the interactive preview popup.

result.name: data_load_result
result.description: When wait=false returns 'accepted' with a jobId. When wait=true returns dataset metadata on success.

jobId.description: Unique job identifier for polling with data_load_status.

path.description: The path that was loaded (present on success).

rowCount.description: Number of data rows (present on success).

type.description: Column type: unknown, scale, ordinal, nominal, or nominalText.

distinctCount.description: Number of distinct values (nominal/ordinal columns only).

methods.name: data_load_status
methods.summary: Poll or block for the status of an async data load job.

params.name: jobId
params.description: The job identifier returned by data_load.

params.name: wait
params.description: If true, blocks until the load finishes or timeoutMs elapses. If false, returns immediately.

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Maximum milliseconds to wait when wait=true.

result.name: data_load_status_result
result.description: Job status plus dataset metadata when status is 'complete'. Same shape as data_info.

path.description: Path to the loaded file (present on complete).

rowCount.description: Number of data rows (present on complete).

methods.name: data_info
methods.summary: Retrieve metadata about the currently loaded dataset. Same shape as data_load (on success) and data_load_status (on complete), but requires no jobId.

result.name: data_info_result
result.description: Metadata about the loaded dataset, or loaded=false if none.

loaded.description: Whether a dataset is currently loaded.

path.description: Path to the currently loaded file.

distinctCount.description: Number of distinct values (nominal/ordinal columns only).

methods.name: analysis_createAnnotation
methods.summary:
Create an annotation analysis that combines result elements from an existing analysis with Markdown text blocks. The annotation keeps the original analysis's form (read-only) so settings are visible but frozen. Use this to add narrative, interpretation, conclusions, or highlight specific results alongside the original output.

Use elements to specify what appears in the annotation and in what order. Each element is either:
  {"name": "tableName"} — pull a result element (table/plot/collection) from the source analysis
  {"md_text": "Markdown/HTML"} — insert a prose block (headings, interpretation, LaTeX math)

If elements is omitted, the annotation starts with a copy of the original analysis's results.

For cross-analysis reports (pulling elements from MULTIPLE analyses), use write_report instead.

params.name: analysisId
params.description: The ID of the existing analysis to annotate. Its results become the default source for named elements that omit sourceAnalysisId.

params.name: title
params.description: Custom title for the annotation. Defaults to 'Annotation [N] of <original title>'.

params.name: elements
params.description:
Ordered array of content elements. Each element is ONE OF:
1. Reference: {"name": "<elementName>"} — pulls a result element (table, plot, collection) from the source analysis. The name must match a .meta entry in the analysis results (e.g. 'ttest', 'descriptives', 'assumptionChecks').
2. Annotation: {"md_text": "<markdown>"} — inserts a Markdown/HTML block for headings, interpretation, conclusions, or LaTeX math.

Examples:
  {"name": "ttest"} — include the t-test table
  {"md_text": "## Key Finding\n\nThe t-test revealed a significant difference..."} — add a section
  {"md_text": "The Bayes factor is $$BF_{10} = 3.42$$"} — display LaTeX math

If omitted or empty, the annotation shows the original analysis results unchanged.

name.description: Name of a result element from the source analysis's .meta array (e.g. 'ttest', 'descriptives', 'assumptionChecks'). Cannot be combined with md_text in the same element.

md_text.description:
Markdown/HTML content. Use for headings (## Section), prose, bullet lists, and LaTeX math. Math is rendered via MathJax: use $$...$$ or \[...\] for display math, and $...$ or \(...\) for inline math.

Examples:
  ## Interpretation
  The groups differ significantly.
  $$P(H|D) = \frac{P(D|H)P(H)}{P(D)}$$
  The effect size was $d = 0.82$.

params.name: status
params.description: Optional status. Defaults to 'complete'.

result.name: analysis_createAnnotation_result
result.description: Metadata about the created annotation, including its ID, module, and analysis name.

analysisId.description: Unique ID of the new annotation analysis.

methods.name: analysis_composeResults
methods.summary:
Reorder, slice, and annotate the results of one or more analyses.

Each element in the 'elements' array is exactly one of:
  { "name": "tableName" }        — include an existing result element by its .meta name (optionally specify sourceAnalysisId to pull from a different analysis)
  { "md_text": "Markdown/HTML" } — insert a Markdown annotation block

The returned results will contain only the elements you specify, in the order you specify them.

params.name: analysisId
params.description: The integer identifier of the target analysis (where the composed results will appear). When an element does not specify its own sourceAnalysisId, it defaults to this value.

params.name: elements
params.description:
Ordered array of element specifications.

Each element is EXACTLY ONE of:
1. Reference:  { "name": "<elementNameFromMeta>"[, "sourceAnalysisId": <id>] }
2. Annotation: { "md_text": "<Markdown/HTML>" }

If sourceAnalysisId is omitted on a reference, the target analysisId is used.
Examples:
  { "name": "ttest" }                              — re-inserts the t-test table from the target analysis
  { "name": "descriptives", "sourceAnalysisId": 43 } — pulls a table from a different analysis
  { "md_text": "## Key Finding\n\nNo significant..." } — inserts a markdown section

name.description: The name of an existing result element from the .meta array (e.g. 'ttest', 'ttestDescriptives'). Mutually exclusive with 'md_text'.

sourceAnalysisId.description: Optional. The analysis ID to pull the named element from. Defaults to the top-level analysisId (target). Use this to compose results from multiple analyses.

md_text.description:
The Markdown/HTML content to display. Required. Must be non-empty.

LaTeX math is supported via MathJax. Use $$...$$ or \[...\] for display math, and $...$ or \(...\) for inline math. Examples: $$P(H|D) = \frac{P(D|H)P(H)}{P(D)}$$ and $p = 0.032$.

params.name: status
params.description: Optional analysis status to apply. Defaults to 'complete'. Valid values: 'complete', 'fatalError'.

result.name: analysis_composeResults_result
result.description: Confirmation that the results were composed successfully.

methods.name: write_report
methods.summary:
Create a new standalone report with content composed from Markdown blocks and cross-analysis result elements. Reports appear in the results panel like analyses but do not run R code.

IMPORTANT: Always prefer referencing existing JASP output elements (tables, plots, collections) via {"name": "<element>", "sourceAnalysisId": <id>} over rewriting them as markdown. Only use md_text for explanatory prose, headings, and narrative — never to recreate statistical results that already exist as proper JASP elements.

params.name: reportId
params.description: If provided, updates an existing report instead of creating a new one. The report's title and results will be replaced.

params.name: title
params.description: Descriptive label for the report. The expander title will be formatted as 'Report: <title>' (or just 'Report' if omitted). Duplicate titles receive automatic suffixes: 'Report: My Findings', 'Report: My Findings 2', etc.

params.name: elements
params.description: Ordered array of element specifications. Each element is either a Markdown block {"md_text": "..."} or a named reference {"name": "...", "sourceAnalysisId": <id>}. Reports have no default source — every named element MUST specify sourceAnalysisId. When omitted, a default welcome markdown block is used.

name.description: Name of an existing result element to pull from the source analysis.

sourceAnalysisId.description: REQUIRED for named elements. The analysis ID to pull the element from.

md_text.description:
Markdown/HTML content to display.

LaTeX math is supported via MathJax. Use $$...$$ or \[...\] for display math, and $...$ or \(...\) for inline math. Examples: $$P(H|D) = \frac{P(D|H)P(H)}{P(D)}$$ and $p = 0.032$.

params.name: status
params.description: Optional analysis status. Defaults to 'complete'.

result.name: write_report_result
result.description: Metadata about the created or updated report.

reportId.description: The report's ID. Use this to reference the report in subsequent write_report calls.

title.description: The report's full title as shown in the results panel.

methods.name: ping
methods.summary: Simple connectivity check. Always returns pong.

methods.name: rpc_discover
methods.summary: Schema discovery. Returns every registered method as an object. Methods with an OpenRPC spec include their full descriptor (summary, params, result); methods without a spec include at minimum their name.

methods.description: List of registered methods, each represented as a method object.

items.description: A method object. At minimum contains 'name'. Methods with an OpenRPC spec also include 'summary', 'params', and 'result'.
